about: Conventional terms and notation with source pointers. A mention is not a verified paper claim. Formulas use their stated assumptions; author notation takes precedence.

entries.label: Softmax
entries.plain: Converts a list of scores into nonnegative weights that total one.
properties: Outputs total one.
Adding the same constant to every input leaves the result unchanged.
entries.caveat: Large weights are not evidence of calibrated confidence.

entries.label: Sigmoid
entries.plain: Maps one real number to a value between zero and one.
properties: Increasing input never decreases output.
entries.caveat: The output is not automatically a trustworthy probability.

entries.label: Gradient
entries.plain: Collects the partial derivatives of a scalar function.
properties: Its coordinates describe local first-order change.
entries.caveat: A local direction does not guarantee finding the best solution.

sources.title: Stanford CS229: linear algebra and matrix calculus

entries.label: Parameters θ
entries.plain: The letter theta often names adjustable model parameters.
properties: A model can have many parameter coordinates.
entries.caveat: Theta can mean something else; check the paper’s definitions.

entries.label: Loss function
entries.plain: Measures an error or objective that training tries to reduce.
properties: The definition determines what counts as a better fit.
entries.caveat: Lower training loss alone does not establish safety or generalization.

entries.label: Expectation 𝔼
entries.plain: A probability-weighted average of a random quantity.
properties: Expectation is linear when the expectations exist.
entries.caveat: The average need not be an outcome you actually observe.

entries.label: Variance
entries.plain: Measures expected squared distance from a mean.
properties: Nonnegative when defined.
entries.caveat: Small variance does not establish a correct mean or an unbiased measurement.

entries.label: Conditional probability
entries.plain: Probability of an event after conditioning on another event.
properties: The event B must have positive probability in this formula.
entries.caveat: Conditioning does not by itself establish causation.

entries.label: Entropy
entries.plain: Summarizes uncertainty in a probability distribution.
properties: The logarithm base sets the unit.
entries.caveat: Higher uncertainty is not the same as more useful knowledge.

sources.title: Deep Learning, chapter 3: probability and information

entries.label: KL divergence
entries.plain: Compares two distributions through expected log probability ratios.
properties: Generally asymmetric.
Nonnegative when defined; can be infinite.
entries.caveat: It is not a symmetric distance metric.

sources.title: Deep Learning, chapter 3: probability and information

entries.label: Attention
entries.plain: Combines value vectors using weights derived from query–key scores.
properties: The scale uses the key dimension in the original formulation.
entries.caveat: Attention weights alone are not a causal explanation of a model.

sources.title: Attention Is All You Need, original paper

entries.label: Transformer
entries.plain: An architecture built around attention and other neural-network components.
entries.formula: token representations → attention and feedforward blocks
properties: The original model uses multiple attention heads.
entries.caveat: An architecture label alone does not establish capabilities or safety.

sources.title: Attention Is All You Need, original paper

entries.label: Sigma σ
entries.plain: An overloaded symbol: it can indicate standard deviation or a sigmoid function.
entries.formula: Meaning depends on the surrounding definition.
properties: No single meaning is safe to infer from the symbol alone.
entries.caveat: Follow the author’s notation rather than choosing a meaning automatically.

entries.label: Summation Σ
entries.plain: Adds the terms indexed below and above a sum sign.
properties: The index tells you which terms are added.
entries.caveat: A finite sum and an infinite series have different assumptions.

sources.title: Stanford CS229: linear algebra and matrix calculus

entries.label: Partial derivative ∂
entries.plain: Rate of change in one input coordinate while holding the other coordinates fixed.
properties: Requires the relevant derivative to exist.
entries.caveat: A partial derivative is a local quantity, not a causal effect.

sources.title: Stanford CS229: linear algebra and matrix calculus

entries.label: Exponential exp
entries.plain: The natural exponential raises the constant e to a real-valued input.
properties: Positive for finite real inputs in exact arithmetic.
entries.caveat: Direct floating-point evaluation can overflow; the explorer uses stable formulas.

entries.label: Logarithm
entries.plain: The inverse of exponentiation for a specified base.
properties: The real natural logarithm needs a positive argument.
entries.caveat: The base determines the scale; do not assume every paper uses the same base.

entries.label: Square root √
entries.plain: The nonnegative real root whose square equals a nonnegative input.
properties: The displayed principal real root is nonnegative.
entries.caveat: Negative real inputs require a different number system or convention.

sources.title: Stanford CS229: linear algebra and matrix calculus

entries.label: Matrix transpose
entries.plain: Swaps a matrix’s row and column indices.
properties: Transposing twice returns the original matrix.
entries.caveat: Transpose is different from inverse and from conjugate transpose.

sources.title: Stanford CS229: linear algebra and matrix calculus

entries.label: Vectors and matrices
entries.plain: A vector holds indexed values; a matrix arranges indexed values in rows and columns.
properties: Matrix multiplication requires compatible inner dimensions.
entries.caveat: A representation’s shape does not tell you what its values mean.

sources.title: Stanford CS229: linear algebra and matrix calculus

entries.label: Queries, keys and values
entries.plain: Attention compares queries with keys to weight the corresponding value representations.
entries.formula: QKᵀ scores → softmax weights → weighted V
properties: Query and key inner dimensions must agree.
entries.caveat: These are representation roles, not a guarantee of a faithful database lookup.

sources.title: Attention Is All You Need, original paper

entries.label: Event intersection ∩
entries.plain: The outcomes shared by two events.
properties: An outcome belongs to both events.
entries.caveat: The intersection is an event, not a probability until a probability measure is applied.

entries.label: Joint-embedding predictive architecture
entries.plain: A JEPA predicts a target representation from a representation of context, rather than rebuilding raw pixels. The representation is a learned collection of numbers, not a guarantee of understanding.
properties: JEPA objectives compare predicted and target embeddings. Avoiding representation collapse and choosing informative context/targets are important design issues; image representation learning, action-free video prediction and action-conditioned planning are different evaluations.
entries.caveat: A research mechanism, not a demonstration of superintelligence. Check the original paper and its evaluation conditions.

entries.label: Recurrent depth
entries.plain: A model can apply a shared processing block repeatedly to refine its hidden state. Extra passes spend inference compute without necessarily writing a longer reasoning trace.
entries.formula: hₖ₊₁ = Fθ(hₖ, context), with shared θ
properties: Weight-tied depth recurrence refines latent states. It is distinct from recurrence across sequence time and from modifying learned weights. Compare accuracy at matched compute, latency and memory, and evaluate stopping criteria and out-of-distribution behavior.
entries.caveat: A research mechanism, not a demonstration of superintelligence. Check the original paper and its evaluation conditions.

entries.label: Latent reasoning
entries.plain: Some systems keep intermediate computation in hidden vectors instead of spelling every step as text. That can change how compute is used, but does not automatically make the result correct or interpretable.
properties: Continuous hidden-state computation differs from a visible chain of thought. Claims need task-specific and compute-matched evaluation; an internal trajectory should not be assumed to be a faithful explanation, nor all latent methods assumed to use recurrent depth.
entries.caveat: A research mechanism, not a demonstration of superintelligence. Check the original paper and its evaluation conditions.

entries.label: World models
entries.plain: A world model predicts selected aspects of an environment and its changes. It may help planning, but can be wrong when actions or situations differ from training.
entries.formula: state representation + action → predicted next representation
properties: Separate observational representation learning from action-conditioned dynamics and closed-loop control. Check interventions, rollout error, distribution shift, safety constraints and whether planning results transfer beyond the evaluated environments.
entries.caveat: A research mechanism, not a demonstration of superintelligence. Check the original paper and its evaluation conditions.
